q: The abdominal muscles can be trained by doing a sit up and a crunch with stretched legs. In which of these exercises will a muscle other than the m. rectus abdominis play an important role?
o: Crunch: internal obliquus and external abdominus m.
e: In a full sit-up the trunk flexes at the hip, so the hip flexors (m. iliopsoas) do much of the work. A crunch only curls the spine and isolates the rectus abdominis more.
s: En un sit-up completo el tronco se flexiona en la cadera, por lo que los flexores de cadera (m. iliopsoas) hacen gran parte del trabajo. Un crunch solo enrolla la columna y aísla más el recto abdominal.

q: What is NOT a movement pattern (plane) of the human body?
e: The three anatomical planes are sagittal, frontal and transverse. 'Diagonal plane' is not one of them.
s: Los tres planos anatómicos son sagital, frontal y transversal. El 'plano diagonal' no es uno de ellos.

q: By flexion we mean...
e: Flexion is bending a joint, which decreases the angle between the bones. Stretching (straightening) a joint is extension.
s: La flexión es doblar una articulación, lo que reduce el ángulo entre los huesos. Estirar una articulación es la extensión.

q: A function of the skeleton is?
e: The skeleton gives the body its shape and support, protects organs, enables movement (as levers), stores minerals and produces blood cells.
s: El esqueleto da forma y soporte al cuerpo, protege los órganos, permite el movimiento (como palancas), almacena minerales y produce células sanguíneas.

q: Skeletal muscle comprises approximately .. % of the total body mass in normal adults.
e: Skeletal muscle makes up roughly 40% of total body mass in a healthy adult.
s: El músculo esquelético constituye aproximadamente el 40% de la masa corporal total en un adulto sano.

q: What kind of joint is the elbow joint?
e: The elbow (humero-ulnar joint) is a hinge joint: it allows flexion and extension in one plane.
s: El codo (articulación húmero-cubital) es una articulación en bisagra: permite flexión y extensión en un solo plano.

q: How are muscles built from large to small?
o: Muscle bundles, muscle fibres, myofibrils, sarcomeres
Myofibrils, sarcomeres, muscle fibres, muscle bundles
Muscle bundles, muscle fibres, sarcomeres, myofibrils
e: Muscle → muscle bundles (fascicles) → muscle fibres (cells) → myofibrils → sarcomeres, the smallest contractile unit.
s: Músculo → haces musculares (fascículos) → fibras musculares (células) → miofibrillas → sarcómeros, la unidad contráctil más pequeña.

q: Bones are grouped into four main categories:
o: Long bones, short bones, flat bones and irregular bones
Long bones, short bones, thin bones, thick bones
e: Bones are classified by shape: long (femur), short (carpals), flat (sternum, skull) and irregular (vertebrae).
s: Los huesos se clasifican por su forma: largos (fémur), cortos (carpos), planos (esternón, cráneo) e irregulares (vértebras).

q: Muscle consists of three types of muscle tissue:
o: Skeletal muscle tissue, cardiac muscle tissue and strength muscle tissue
Skeletal muscle tissue, cardiac muscle tissue and smooth muscle tissue
Skeletal muscle tissue, cardio muscle tissue and smooth muscle tissue
Energy muscle tissue, cardiac muscle tissue and smooth muscle tissue
e: The three types are skeletal (voluntary, striated), cardiac (heart) and smooth (organs, blood vessels). Watch the wording: 'cardiac', not 'cardio'.
s: Los tres tipos son esquelético (voluntario, estriado), cardíaco (corazón) y liso (órganos, vasos sanguíneos). Ojo con la palabra: 'cardíaco', no 'cardio'.

q: What is NOT a role of the skeletal muscle?
o: To hold or move the body and its segments
To move blood around the body
e: Moving blood around the body is the job of the heart (cardiac muscle). Skeletal muscle moves and holds the body, maintains posture and produces heat.
s: Mover la sangre por el cuerpo es la función del corazón (músculo cardíaco). El músculo esquelético mueve y sostiene el cuerpo, mantiene la postura y produce calor.

q: What is the smallest contractile unit of a muscle?
e: The sarcomere, made of actin and myosin filaments, is the smallest functional unit that contracts.
s: El sarcómero, formado por filamentos de actina y miosina, es la unidad funcional más pequeña que se contrae.

q: Which two protein filaments slide over each other during a muscle contraction?
e: According to the sliding filament theory, myosin heads pull the actin filaments toward the centre of the sarcomere.
s: Según la teoría de los filamentos deslizantes, las cabezas de miosina tiran de los filamentos de actina hacia el centro del sarcómero.

q: By extension we mean...
o: Moving a limb away from the midline
e: Extension straightens a joint and increases the angle between the bones; it is the opposite of flexion.
s: La extensión endereza una articulación y aumenta el ángulo entre los huesos; es lo contrario de la flexión.

q: Moving a limb away from the midline of the body is called...
e: Abduction moves away from the midline (e.g. lateral raise). Adduction 'adds' the limb back to the body.
s: La abducción aleja el miembro de la línea media (p. ej., elevación lateral). La aducción lo acerca de nuevo al cuerpo.

q: In which plane does a lateral raise take place?
e: Sideways movements (abduction/adduction) happen in the frontal plane, which divides the body into front and back.
s: Los movimientos laterales (abducción/aducción) ocurren en el plano frontal, que divide el cuerpo en parte anterior y posterior.

q: In which plane does a squat or a biceps curl mainly take place?
e: Forward and backward movements (flexion/extension) take place in the sagittal plane, which divides the body into left and right.
s: Los movimientos hacia delante y atrás (flexión/extensión) ocurren en el plano sagital, que divide el cuerpo en izquierda y derecha.

q: A trunk rotation (e.g. a wood chop or Russian twist) takes place mainly in the...
e: Rotations take place in the transverse (horizontal) plane, which divides the body into upper and lower halves.
s: Las rotaciones ocurren en el plano transversal (horizontal), que divide el cuerpo en mitad superior e inferior.

q: What type of joint is the shoulder joint?
e: The shoulder (glenohumeral) joint is a ball-and-socket joint and allows movement in all three planes.
s: El hombro (articulación glenohumeral) es una articulación esférica (enartrosis) y permite movimiento en los tres planos.

q: Which joint is a saddle joint?
e: The carpometacarpal joint of the thumb is the classic saddle joint, which lets the thumb oppose the fingers.
s: La articulación carpometacarpiana del pulgar es la articulación en silla de montar típica; permite oponer el pulgar a los dedos.

q: The joint between the first and second cervical vertebrae (atlas and axis), which lets you shake your head 'no', is a...
e: The atlanto-axial joint is a pivot joint and allows rotation only.
s: La articulación atlantoaxial es una articulación en pivote y solo permite rotación.

q: Which muscle is the agonist during a biceps curl?
e: The agonist (prime mover) produces the movement: the biceps brachii flexes the elbow. The triceps is the antagonist.
s: El agonista (motor principal) produce el movimiento: el bíceps braquial flexiona el codo. El tríceps es el antagonista.

q: What is the antagonist of the m. quadriceps femoris during a knee extension?
e: The antagonist performs the opposite movement. The hamstrings flex the knee, so they oppose the quadriceps.
s: El antagonista realiza el movimiento opuesto. Los isquiotibiales flexionan la rodilla, por lo que se oponen al cuádriceps.

q: Which muscle group is primarily responsible for hip extension?
e: The gluteus maximus and hamstrings extend the hip, for example when standing up from a squat or during a deadlift.
s: El glúteo mayor y los isquiotibiales extienden la cadera, por ejemplo al levantarse de una sentadilla o en el peso muerto.

q: Which muscle is the main hip flexor?
e: The iliopsoas (psoas major + iliacus) is the strongest hip flexor.
s: El iliopsoas (psoas mayor + ilíaco) es el flexor de cadera más potente.

q: Which part of the quadriceps also crosses the hip joint?
e: The rectus femoris is a two-joint (bi-articular) muscle: it extends the knee and also flexes the hip.
s: El recto femoral es un músculo biarticular: extiende la rodilla y además flexiona la cadera.

q: Which muscle forms most of the calf and plantar-flexes the ankle?
e: The gastrocnemius (with the soleus) plantar-flexes the ankle, as in a calf raise. The tibialis anterior does the opposite (dorsiflexion).
s: El gastrocnemio (junto con el sóleo) realiza la flexión plantar del tobillo, como en una elevación de talones. El tibial anterior hace lo contrario (dorsiflexión).

q: Which muscle is mainly trained with a lat pulldown?
e: The latissimus dorsi adducts and extends the upper arm, which is the pulling-down movement of the lat pulldown.
s: El dorsal ancho aduce y extiende el brazo, que es el movimiento de tirar hacia abajo en el jalón al pecho.

q: Which muscle keeps the spine upright and extends the back?
e: The erector spinae runs along the spine and extends it; it is important for posture.
s: El erector de la columna recorre la columna vertebral y la extiende; es importante para la postura.

q: Which abdominal muscle acts like a natural 'corset' and is important for core stability?
e: The transversus abdominis is the deepest abdominal muscle; it wraps around the trunk and raises intra-abdominal pressure to stabilise the spine.
s: El transverso del abdomen es el músculo abdominal más profundo; rodea el tronco y aumenta la presión intraabdominal para estabilizar la columna.

q: What connects a muscle to a bone?
e: Tendons connect muscle to bone. Ligaments connect bone to bone.
s: Los tendones conectan el músculo con el hueso. Los ligamentos conectan hueso con hueso.

q: What connects bone to bone and stabilises a joint?
e: Ligaments connect bones to each other and give stability to joints.
s: Los ligamentos unen los huesos entre sí y dan estabilidad a las articulaciones.

q: How many vertebrae does the cervical spine have?
e: Cervical 7, thoracic 12, lumbar 5, then the sacrum and coccyx.
s: Cervicales 7, torácicas 12, lumbares 5, después el sacro y el cóccix.

q: How many thoracic vertebrae are there?
e: There are 12 thoracic vertebrae; each connects to a pair of ribs.
s: Hay 12 vértebras torácicas; cada una se une a un par de costillas.

q: The natural forward curve of the lumbar spine is called...
e: Lordosis is the natural inward (forward) curve in the neck and lower back. Kyphosis is the outward curve of the thoracic spine. Scoliosis is a sideways curve.
s: La lordosis es la curva natural hacia dentro (hacia delante) del cuello y la zona lumbar. La cifosis es la curva hacia fuera de la columna torácica. La escoliosis es una curva lateral.

q: An abnormal sideways curvature of the spine is called...
e: Scoliosis is a lateral (sideways) curvature of the spine, often with rotation.
s: La escoliosis es una curvatura lateral de la columna, a menudo con rotación.

q: What is the longest and strongest bone in the human body?
e: The femur (thigh bone) is the longest and strongest bone.
s: El fémur (hueso del muslo) es el hueso más largo y fuerte.

q: Which muscle fibre type is best suited for endurance activities?
e: Type I (slow-twitch, red) fibres have many mitochondria and capillaries, use oxygen and fatigue slowly.
s: Las fibras tipo I (lentas, rojas) tienen muchas mitocondrias y capilares, usan oxígeno y se fatigan lentamente.

q: Which statement about type II (fast-twitch) muscle fibres is correct?
o: They produce a lot of force quickly but fatigue fast
They are mainly used at rest
e: Fast-twitch fibres contract quickly and forcefully, rely more on anaerobic energy and tire quickly. Sprinters have a high proportion.
s: Las fibras rápidas se contraen con rapidez y fuerza, dependen más de la energía anaeróbica y se cansan pronto. Los velocistas tienen una gran proporción.

q: A muscle contraction in which the muscle lengthens under tension is called...
e: Eccentric = lengthening under load (e.g. lowering the bar in a curl). Concentric = shortening. Isometric = no change in length.
s: Excéntrica = alargamiento bajo carga (p. ej., bajar la barra en un curl). Concéntrica = acortamiento. Isométrica = sin cambio de longitud.

q: Holding a plank is an example of which type of muscle contraction?
e: In an isometric contraction the muscle produces force without changing length and without joint movement.
s: En una contracción isométrica el músculo produce fuerza sin cambiar de longitud y sin movimiento articular.

q: Turning the palm of the hand downward is called...
e: Pronation turns the palm down (or back). Supination turns the palm up, as if holding a bowl of soup.
s: La pronación gira la palma hacia abajo (o atrás). La supinación gira la palma hacia arriba, como si sostuvieras un plato de sopa.

q: Which term describes a position closer to the trunk or point of attachment?
e: Proximal = closer to the trunk/origin; distal = further away. The elbow is proximal to the wrist.
s: Proximal = más cerca del tronco/origen; distal = más lejos. El codo es proximal respecto a la muñeca.

q: Where in the body are red blood cells produced?
e: Red blood cells are produced in the red bone marrow (haematopoiesis), one of the functions of the skeleton.
s: Los glóbulos rojos se producen en la médula ósea roja (hematopoyesis), una de las funciones del esqueleto.

q: Which joint type allows the most freedom of movement?
e: Ball-and-socket joints (shoulder, hip) move in all three planes, so they have the largest range of motion.
s: Las articulaciones esféricas (hombro, cadera) se mueven en los tres planos, por lo que tienen la mayor amplitud de movimiento.

q: EPOC stands for
e: EPOC = Excess Post-exercise Oxygen Consumption: the extra oxygen used after exercise to restore the body (refill CP stores, clear lactate, cool down). Note the trap words 'Extra' and the missing 'consumption'.
s: EPOC = consumo excesivo de oxígeno post-ejercicio: el oxígeno extra que se usa después del ejercicio para recuperar el cuerpo (reponer la fosfocreatina, eliminar lactato, enfriarse). Cuidado con las trampas 'Extra' y la falta de 'consumption'.

q: What is ADP?
o: A residue after cleavage of ATP
e: When ATP releases energy, one phosphate group splits off and ADP (adenosine diphosphate) remains. ADP is then rebuilt into ATP.
s: Cuando el ATP libera energía, se separa un grupo fosfato y queda ADP (adenosín difosfato). Después el ADP se vuelve a convertir en ATP.

q: What substance is produced during the anaerobic breakdown of glucose in the muscle fibre?
e: Without enough oxygen, glucose is broken down to pyruvate and then lactic acid (lactate). CO2 and H2O are the products of aerobic breakdown.
s: Sin suficiente oxígeno, la glucosa se descompone en piruvato y luego en ácido láctico (lactato). El CO2 y el H2O son los productos de la vía aeróbica.

q: What is ATP?
o: The direct energy source for muscle contraction
A hormone that regulates blood sugar
A waste product of fat burning
e: ATP (adenosine triphosphate) is the only direct energy source for muscle contraction. All energy systems exist to rebuild ATP.
s: El ATP (adenosín trifosfato) es la única fuente directa de energía para la contracción muscular. Todos los sistemas energéticos existen para regenerar ATP.

q: How long does the ATP-CP (phosphagen) system supply energy at maximal effort?
e: Stored ATP and creatine phosphate deliver energy very fast but only for roughly 6–10 seconds of maximal effort, e.g. a 60 m sprint or a heavy single lift.
s: El ATP almacenado y la fosfocreatina aportan energía muy rápido pero solo durante unos 6–10 segundos de esfuerzo máximo, p. ej., un sprint de 60 m o un levantamiento pesado.

q: Which energy system dominates during a 400 m sprint (about 50–60 seconds)?
e: Maximal efforts of roughly 10 seconds to 2 minutes rely mainly on anaerobic glycolysis, which produces lactate.
s: Los esfuerzos máximos de unos 10 segundos a 2 minutos dependen sobre todo de la glucólisis anaeróbica, que produce lactato.

q: Which energy system is used mainly during a 45-minute easy run?
e: Long, moderate efforts are fuelled aerobically: carbohydrates and fats are broken down with oxygen in the mitochondria.
s: Los esfuerzos largos y moderados se alimentan aeróbicamente: los carbohidratos y las grasas se descomponen con oxígeno en las mitocondrias.

q: What are the end products of the aerobic breakdown of glucose?
e: With oxygen, glucose is fully broken down to carbon dioxide, water and a large amount of ATP.
s: Con oxígeno, la glucosa se descompone por completo en dióxido de carbono, agua y una gran cantidad de ATP.

q: In which part of the muscle cell does aerobic energy production take place?
e: The mitochondria are the 'power plants' of the cell, where aerobic ATP production takes place.
s: Las mitocondrias son las 'centrales eléctricas' de la célula, donde se produce el ATP de forma aeróbica.

q: Which energy system delivers energy the fastest?
e: The ATP-CP system is the fastest (one chemical step) but has the smallest capacity. The aerobic system is the slowest but has the largest capacity.
s: El sistema ATP-PC es el más rápido (un solo paso químico) pero tiene la menor capacidad. El sistema aeróbico es el más lento pero tiene la mayor capacidad.

q: What does VO2max indicate?
o: Maximum amount of oxygen the body can take up and use per minute
e: VO2max is the maximal oxygen uptake (ml/kg/min), the best single indicator of aerobic (cardiorespiratory) fitness.
s: El VO2max es el consumo máximo de oxígeno (ml/kg/min), el mejor indicador individual de la capacidad aeróbica (cardiorrespiratoria).

q: Which formula is commonly used to estimate maximum heart rate?
e: HRmax ≈ 220 − age. It is an estimate with a spread of about ±10–12 beats.
s: FCmáx ≈ 220 − edad. Es una estimación con un margen de unos ±10–12 latidos.

q: Cardiac output is...
e: Cardiac output (litres per minute) = heart rate × stroke volume (the amount of blood pumped per beat).
s: El gasto cardíaco (litros por minuto) = frecuencia cardíaca × volumen sistólico (la cantidad de sangre bombeada por latido).

q: What is a typical long-term effect of endurance training on resting heart rate?
e: Endurance training enlarges the stroke volume, so the heart needs fewer beats at rest to pump the same amount of blood.
s: El entrenamiento de resistencia aumenta el volumen sistólico, así que el corazón necesita menos latidos en reposo para bombear la misma cantidad de sangre.

q: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?
e: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry it back. Gas exchange takes place in the capillaries.
s: Las arterias llevan la sangre desde el corazón; las venas la devuelven. El intercambio de gases ocurre en los capilares.

q: Where does gas exchange between the lungs and the blood take place?
e: Oxygen and CO2 are exchanged in the alveoli, tiny air sacs surrounded by capillaries.
s: El oxígeno y el CO2 se intercambian en los alvéolos, pequeños sacos de aire rodeados de capilares.

q: What is the main breathing muscle?
e: The diaphragm contracts and flattens during inhalation, which draws air into the lungs.
s: El diafragma se contrae y se aplana durante la inspiración, lo que hace entrar aire en los pulmones.

q: Which substance in the blood transports oxygen?
e: Haemoglobin in the red blood cells binds oxygen and carries it to the tissues.
s: La hemoglobina de los glóbulos rojos se une al oxígeno y lo transporta a los tejidos.

q: What is the anaerobic (lactate) threshold?
o: The point at which fat burning stops completely
The intensity above which lactate builds up faster than it can be removed
The maximum amount of weight you can lift
e: Above the lactate threshold, lactate production exceeds clearance, so it accumulates and fatigue follows quickly.
s: Por encima del umbral de lactato, la producción supera la eliminación, el lactato se acumula y la fatiga llega rápido.

q: In which form are carbohydrates stored in the muscles and liver?
e: Carbohydrate is stored as glycogen in muscle and liver. Fat is stored as triglycerides.
s: Los carbohidratos se almacenan como glucógeno en el músculo y el hígado. La grasa se almacena como triglicéridos.

q: Which hormone lowers blood sugar levels?
e: Insulin (from the pancreas) helps cells take up glucose, which lowers blood sugar. Glucagon raises it.
s: La insulina (del páncreas) ayuda a las células a absorber la glucosa, lo que reduce el azúcar en sangre. El glucagón lo eleva.

q: What is supercompensation?
o: Eating extra carbohydrates before a match
Overtraining caused by too little rest
Recovery to a level above the starting level after training and rest
e: After training load (fatigue) and adequate recovery, the body adapts above its previous level. Training again at that moment leads to progress.
s: Tras la carga de entrenamiento (fatiga) y una recuperación adecuada, el cuerpo se adapta por encima de su nivel anterior. Volver a entrenar en ese momento produce progreso.

q: What is the main cause of muscle hypertrophy?
o: An increase in the size (cross-section) of existing muscle fibres
An increase in the number of muscle fibres
e: Hypertrophy mainly means existing fibres get thicker through more myofibrils and contractile proteins.
s: La hipertrofia significa principalmente que las fibras existentes se engrosan por un aumento de miofibrillas y proteínas contráctiles.

q: Strength gains in the first weeks of a strength training programme are mainly caused by...
e: Early gains (roughly the first 4–8 weeks) come mainly from the nervous system: more motor units recruited and better coordination. Hypertrophy follows later.
s: Las mejoras iniciales (aproximadamente las primeras 4–8 semanas) vienen sobre todo del sistema nervioso: se reclutan más unidades motoras y mejora la coordinación. La hipertrofia llega después.

q: A motor unit consists of...
o: The brain and the spinal cord
One motor neuron and all the muscle fibres it innervates
e: A motor unit is one motor neuron plus all the muscle fibres it controls. More force = more and larger motor units recruited.
s: Una unidad motora es una motoneurona más todas las fibras musculares que controla. Más fuerza = se reclutan más unidades motoras y más grandes.

q: Which statement about lactate (lactic acid) is correct?
o: It is only produced at rest
It is produced during anaerobic glycolysis and can be reused as fuel
It is produced in the ATP-CP system
It causes muscle soreness 2 days after training (DOMS)
e: Lactate is a by-product of anaerobic glycolysis and is reused as fuel (by the heart, muscles and liver). DOMS is caused by micro-damage, not lactate.
s: El lactato es un subproducto de la glucólisis anaeróbica y se reutiliza como combustible (corazón, músculos, hígado). Las agujetas (DOMS) se deben a microlesiones, no al lactato.

q: What is DOMS?
e: DOMS = Delayed Onset Muscle Soreness, the stiffness that peaks 24–72 hours after unaccustomed (especially eccentric) exercise.
s: DOMS = dolor muscular de aparición tardía (agujetas), la rigidez que alcanza su máximo 24–72 horas después de un ejercicio no habitual (sobre todo excéntrico).

q: Which type of contraction causes the most muscle soreness (DOMS)?
e: Eccentric contractions (e.g. downhill running, lowering weights) cause the most micro-damage and therefore the most DOMS.
s: Las contracciones excéntricas (p. ej., correr cuesta abajo, bajar pesos) causan más microlesiones y, por tanto, más agujetas.

q: What is the normal resting heart rate range for an adult?
e: Normal resting heart rate is about 60–100 beats per minute. Well-trained endurance athletes can be lower.
s: La frecuencia cardíaca normal en reposo es de unos 60–100 latidos por minuto. Los deportistas de resistencia entrenados pueden tenerla más baja.

q: Which blood pressure value is considered normal/optimal for adults?
e: Around 120/80 mmHg (systolic/diastolic) is normal. 140/90 or higher is generally classed as high blood pressure (hypertension).
s: Alrededor de 120/80 mmHg (sistólica/diastólica) es normal. 140/90 o más se clasifica generalmente como hipertensión.

q: The systolic blood pressure is the pressure...
e: Systolic = pressure during contraction of the heart (upper number). Diastolic = pressure during relaxation (lower number).
s: Sistólica = presión durante la contracción del corazón (número superior). Diastólica = presión durante la relajación (número inferior).

q: Which macronutrient is the main fuel at rest and during low-intensity exercise?
e: At rest and low intensity, fat supplies most of the energy. As intensity rises, carbohydrate takes over.
s: En reposo y a baja intensidad, la grasa aporta la mayor parte de la energía. Al aumentar la intensidad, los carbohidratos toman el relevo.

q: What happens to blood flow to the working muscles during exercise?
e: During exercise blood is redirected to working muscles (vasodilation there, less to the digestive organs).
s: Durante el ejercicio la sangre se redirige a los músculos activos (vasodilatación allí y menos flujo a los órganos digestivos).

q: Creatine phosphate is used to...
e: Creatine phosphate donates its phosphate to ADP, rebuilding ATP very quickly at the start of intense effort.
s: La fosfocreatina cede su fosfato al ADP y regenera ATP muy rápidamente al inicio de un esfuerzo intenso.

q: The definition of biomechanics is?
o: Indicating the difference between strength, load and being strong
Calculating the magnitude and direction of the force
Creating training schedules with the help of different forces
The doctrine of forces and the effect of forces on the human body
e: Biomechanics is the study of forces and their effects on the human body (movement, loading of joints and tissues).
s: La biomecánica es el estudio de las fuerzas y sus efectos sobre el cuerpo humano (movimiento, carga de articulaciones y tejidos).

q: How does overloading occur?
o: The load is equal to the load capacity
The load is higher than the load capacity
The load capacity is greater than the load
The load is lower than the load capacity
e: Overload (overbelasting) happens when the load is greater than what the tissue or person can handle (the load capacity). This can lead to injury.
s: La sobrecarga ocurre cuando la carga es mayor que lo que el tejido o la persona puede soportar (la capacidad de carga). Puede provocar lesiones.

q: What is load capacity (belastbaarheid)?
o: The total training volume per week
The number of repetitions in a set
The amount of load a person or tissue can handle without damage
e: Load capacity is what the body or a tissue can tolerate. Good training keeps load slightly above current level, then lets capacity grow with recovery.
s: La capacidad de carga es lo que el cuerpo o un tejido puede tolerar. Un buen entrenamiento mantiene la carga ligeramente por encima del nivel actual y deja que la capacidad crezca con la recuperación.

q: Which factor lowers a person's load capacity?
e: Fatigue, stress, poor sleep, illness and previous injury reduce load capacity, so the same load is more likely to cause overload.
s: La fatiga, el estrés, dormir mal, la enfermedad y las lesiones previas reducen la capacidad de carga, así que la misma carga tiene más probabilidad de causar sobrecarga.

q: A force is described by its...
o: Size (magnitude), direction and point of application
e: A force is a vector: it has a magnitude, a direction and a point of application.
s: Una fuerza es un vector: tiene magnitud, dirección y punto de aplicación.

q: In what unit is force expressed?
e: Force is measured in Newtons (N). 1 kg of mass weighs roughly 10 N on Earth.
s: La fuerza se mide en newtons (N). 1 kg de masa pesa aproximadamente 10 N en la Tierra.

q: Newton's second law states that...
o: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction
An object stays at rest unless a force acts on it
e: F = m × a. The first law is inertia; the third is action = reaction.
s: F = m × a. La primera ley es la inercia; la tercera es acción = reacción.

q: When you push off the ground while running, the ground pushes back on you. Which law is this?
e: Newton's third law: every action has an equal and opposite reaction (ground reaction force).
s: Tercera ley de Newton: a toda acción le corresponde una reacción igual y opuesta (fuerza de reacción del suelo).

q: What is a moment (torque)?
e: Moment (torque) = force × moment arm (the perpendicular distance from the line of force to the axis of rotation).
s: El momento (par de fuerza) = fuerza × brazo de momento (la distancia perpendicular de la línea de fuerza al eje de rotación).

q: During a lateral raise, when is the load on the shoulder greatest?
o: The load is the same throughout
At the start of the movement
e: The moment arm of the dumbbell is longest when the arm is horizontal, so the torque on the shoulder is highest there.
s: El brazo de momento de la mancuerna es máximo cuando el brazo está horizontal, por lo que el par sobre el hombro es mayor en ese punto.

q: How can you make a push-up easier without changing the exercise?
o: Do it from the knees (shorter lever)
Put the feet on a bench
e: From the knees the lever (body length) is shorter and less body weight is lifted, which lowers the load.
s: Desde las rodillas la palanca (longitud del cuerpo) es más corta y se levanta menos peso corporal, lo que reduce la carga.

q: In a squat, which change increases the load (moment) on the lower back?
e: Leaning forward moves the bar further from the hip and spine axis, so the moment arm and the load on the lower back increase.
s: Inclinarse hacia delante aleja la barra del eje de la cadera y la columna, de modo que aumentan el brazo de momento y la carga en la zona lumbar.

q: A lever system consists of...
e: Every lever has an axis/fulcrum (the joint), an effort (muscle force) and a resistance (load). In the body, bones are the levers.
s: Toda palanca tiene un eje o punto de apoyo (la articulación), una potencia (fuerza muscular) y una resistencia (carga). En el cuerpo, los huesos son las palancas.

q: Most levers in the human body (e.g. the elbow during a biceps curl) are...
e: In a third-class lever the effort lies between the axis and the load. This favours speed and range of motion over force.
s: En una palanca de tercer grado la potencia está entre el eje y la carga. Favorece la velocidad y la amplitud de movimiento frente a la fuerza.

q: Standing on your toes (calf raise) is often given as an example of a...
e: In a calf raise the axis is the ball of the foot, the load (body weight) is in the middle and the effort (calf) is at the heel: a second-class lever.
s: En una elevación de talones el eje es la parte anterior del pie, la carga (peso corporal) está en el medio y la potencia (gemelo) en el talón: palanca de segundo grado.

q: Nodding the head (the neck joint as axis between head weight and neck muscles) is an example of a...
e: In a first-class lever the axis lies between effort and load, like a seesaw.
s: En una palanca de primer grado el eje está entre la potencia y la carga, como un balancín.

q: When is a person most stable?
o: Large base of support and low centre of gravity
Small base of support and high centre of gravity
Centre of gravity outside the base of support
e: Stability increases with a wider base of support, a lower centre of gravity and the centre of gravity well within the base.
s: La estabilidad aumenta con una base de apoyo más amplia, un centro de gravedad más bajo y el centro de gravedad bien dentro de la base.

q: Where is the centre of gravity of a standing adult roughly located?
o: At the level of the head
Around the navel / just in front of the sacrum
e: In upright standing the centre of gravity lies roughly at navel height, just in front of the second sacral vertebra.
s: De pie, el centro de gravedad está aproximadamente a la altura del ombligo, justo delante de la segunda vértebra sacra.

q: Which type of load on tissue is caused by forces pulling in opposite directions?
e: Tension pulls tissue apart; compression pushes it together; shear makes layers slide; torsion twists.
s: La tensión (tracción) separa el tejido; la compresión lo junta; el cizallamiento hace deslizar las capas; la torsión lo retuerce.

q: Speed × mass equals...
e: Momentum = mass × velocity. Power = work ÷ time. Work = force × distance.
s: Cantidad de movimiento = masa × velocidad. Potencia = trabajo ÷ tiempo. Trabajo = fuerza × distancia.

q: Power is defined as...
e: Power is the rate of doing work: work ÷ time, or force × velocity. Explosive movements require high power.
s: La potencia es la rapidez con la que se realiza un trabajo: trabajo ÷ tiempo, o fuerza × velocidad. Los movimientos explosivos requieren mucha potencia.

q: Why does a cable machine give a different strength curve than a free weight?
o: The direction of resistance follows the cable, not gravity
Gravity always pulls the cable down
e: With free weights resistance always acts vertically (gravity). With cables, resistance follows the cable line, so the hardest point of the movement changes.
s: Con peso libre la resistencia siempre actúa en vertical (gravedad). Con poleas, la resistencia sigue la línea del cable, así que el punto más difícil del movimiento cambia.

q: What is the effect of a longer lever arm with the same weight?
e: Torque = force × lever arm. Longer arm, same weight → more torque, so the exercise feels heavier (e.g. straight-arm vs bent-arm fly).
s: Par = fuerza × brazo de palanca. Brazo más largo con el mismo peso → más par, así que el ejercicio se siente más pesado (p. ej., aperturas con brazos rectos frente a flexionados).

q: Load and load capacity are in balance. What happens if you train regularly with a load slightly above the current capacity and allow recovery?
e: A load slightly above capacity followed by recovery stimulates adaptation, so load capacity grows (principle of progressive overload).
s: Una carga ligeramente superior a la capacidad seguida de recuperación estimula la adaptación, así que la capacidad de carga aumenta (principio de sobrecarga progresiva).

q: Which statement about friction is correct?
o: Friction is a force that opposes sliding between two surfaces
e: Friction resists sliding between surfaces. Good shoe grip uses friction; a slippery floor lacks it.
s: La fricción se opone al deslizamiento entre superficies. El buen agarre de una zapatilla usa la fricción; un suelo resbaladizo carece de ella.

q: A deadlift with the bar far from the shins is riskier because...
o: The moment arm to the lower back increases
e: The further the bar is from the body, the longer the moment arm around the hip and spine, which increases load on the lower back.
s: Cuanto más lejos esté la barra del cuerpo, más largo es el brazo de momento alrededor de la cadera y la columna, lo que aumenta la carga en la zona lumbar.

q: What is inertia?
o: The speed of a falling object
The tendency of an object to resist a change in its state of motion
e: Inertia (Newton's first law): an object stays at rest or in uniform motion unless a force acts on it. More mass = more inertia.
s: Inercia (primera ley de Newton): un objeto permanece en reposo o en movimiento uniforme a menos que actúe una fuerza sobre él. Más masa = más inercia.

q: What is a closed kinetic chain exercise?
o: An exercise in which the hand or foot moves freely (e.g. leg extension)
An exercise performed on a machine only
An exercise in which the hand or foot is fixed against a surface (e.g. squat, push-up)
e: Closed chain: distal segment fixed (squat, push-up). Open chain: distal segment free (leg extension, biceps curl).
s: Cadena cerrada: segmento distal fijo (sentadilla, flexión). Cadena abierta: segmento distal libre (extensión de pierna, curl de bíceps).

q: A leg extension on a machine is an example of...
e: In a leg extension the foot moves freely, so it is an open kinetic chain exercise.
s: En una extensión de pierna el pie se mueve libremente, así que es un ejercicio de cadena cinética abierta.

q: What does the training principle 'specificity' mean?
o: You should always train with heavy weights
Training must be varied every session
Every training gives the same result
The body adapts specifically to the type of load it is given
e: Specificity: adaptations match the training stimulus. A marathon runner should mainly train endurance, not maximal strength.
s: Especificidad: las adaptaciones corresponden al estímulo de entrenamiento. Un maratoniano debe entrenar sobre todo la resistencia, no la fuerza máxima.

q: What does the principle of 'reversibility' mean?
o: Exercises can be done in reverse order
Training effects disappear when training stops
Heavier training always gives faster results
You can reverse an injury by training
e: Reversibility ('use it or lose it'): when you stop training, adaptations gradually decline.
s: Reversibilidad ('lo que no se usa se pierde'): cuando dejas de entrenar, las adaptaciones disminuyen poco a poco.

q: What does 'progressive overload' mean?
o: Training more than twice a day
Gradually increasing the training load as the body adapts
e: Progressive overload: increase load (weight, reps, sets, intensity, duration) step by step to keep stimulating adaptation.
s: Sobrecarga progresiva: aumentar la carga (peso, repeticiones, series, intensidad, duración) poco a poco para seguir estimulando la adaptación.

q: What does FITT stand for?
e: FITT = Frequency, Intensity, Time (duration), Type. These are the variables you adjust in a training programme.
s: FITT = Frecuencia, Intensidad, Tiempo (duración), Tipo. Son las variables que se ajustan en un programa de entrenamiento.

q: Which repetition range is most suitable for training maximal strength?
e: Maximal strength is trained with heavy loads (about 85%+ of 1RM) for 1–5 reps and long rests.
s: La fuerza máxima se entrena con cargas altas (aprox. 85%+ del 1RM) en 1–5 repeticiones y descansos largos.

q: Which repetition range is classically recommended for hypertrophy (muscle growth)?
e: The classic hypertrophy zone is about 6–12 reps at roughly 65–85% of 1RM, with moderate rests (about 60–90 s).
s: La zona clásica de hipertrofia es de unas 6–12 repeticiones al 65–85% del 1RM, con descansos moderados (unos 60–90 s).

q: Which repetition range fits muscular endurance training?
e: Muscular endurance is trained with lighter loads (below about 65% 1RM) and high reps (15+), with short rests.
s: La resistencia muscular se entrena con cargas ligeras (por debajo del 65% del 1RM) y muchas repeticiones (15+), con descansos cortos.

q: What does 1RM mean?
o: The maximum weight you can lift once with good technique
The minimum weight for a warm-up
e: 1RM (one repetition maximum) is the heaviest load you can lift for a single correct repetition. Training loads are often given as a % of 1RM.
s: El 1RM (una repetición máxima) es la carga más pesada que puedes levantar en una sola repetición correcta. Las cargas suelen expresarse como % del 1RM.

q: What rest between sets is appropriate for maximal strength training?
e: Heavy maximal strength sets need 2–5 minutes so the ATP-CP system can recover.
s: Las series pesadas de fuerza máxima necesitan 2–5 minutos para que el sistema ATP-PC se recupere.

q: What is periodisation?
o: Systematically planning training in phases (cycles) with different goals
Training at the same intensity all year
e: Periodisation divides training into macro-, meso- and microcycles with changing goals, volume and intensity to optimise progress and prevent overtraining.
s: La periodización divide el entrenamiento en macro-, meso- y microciclos con objetivos, volumen e intensidad cambiantes para optimizar el progreso y evitar el sobreentrenamiento.

q: A microcycle usually lasts...
e: Microcycle ≈ 1 week; mesocycle ≈ several weeks (often 3–6); macrocycle ≈ a season or a year.
s: Microciclo ≈ 1 semana; mesociclo ≈ varias semanas (a menudo 3–6); macrociclo ≈ una temporada o un año.

q: What is the order of the training cycles from largest to smallest?
e: Macro (largest, e.g. a year) → meso (block of weeks) → micro (a week).
s: Macro (el más grande, p. ej., un año) → meso (bloque de semanas) → micro (una semana).

q: Which is a sign of overtraining?
o: Persistent fatigue, declining performance and a raised resting heart rate
Lower resting heart rate and better sleep
e: Overtraining shows as lasting fatigue, falling performance, raised resting heart rate, poor sleep, irritability and more illness.
s: El sobreentrenamiento se manifiesta como fatiga persistente, bajada del rendimiento, frecuencia cardíaca en reposo elevada, mal sueño, irritabilidad y más enfermedades.

q: The Karvonen formula uses...
e: Karvonen: target HR = HRrest + (HRmax − HRrest) × intensity %. It accounts for individual resting heart rate.
s: Karvonen: FC objetivo = FCreposo + (FCmáx − FCreposo) × % de intensidad. Tiene en cuenta la frecuencia cardíaca en reposo individual.

q: A 40-year-old client has a resting heart rate of 60. Using Karvonen, what is the target heart rate at 70% intensity?
e: HRmax = 220 − 40 = 180. Reserve = 180 − 60 = 120. 120 × 0.7 = 84. Target = 60 + 84 = 144 bpm. (126 bpm is 70% of HRmax, the simple method without the resting heart rate.)

q: What does RPE stand for?
e: RPE = Rate (Rating) of Perceived Exertion, e.g. the Borg scale (6–20) or a 1–10 scale.
s: RPE = escala de esfuerzo percibido, p. ej., la escala de Borg (6–20) o una escala de 1–10.

q: The original Borg scale runs from...
e: The original Borg RPE scale runs from 6 to 20 (roughly heart rate ÷ 10). The modified CR10 scale runs from 0 to 10.
s: La escala de Borg original va de 6 a 20 (aproximadamente frecuencia cardíaca ÷ 10). La escala CR10 modificada va de 0 a 10.

q: What is interval training?
o: Alternating periods of high intensity with periods of rest or low intensity
e: Interval training alternates work and recovery bouts, allowing more time at high intensity than continuous training.
s: El entrenamiento por intervalos alterna fases de trabajo y recuperación, lo que permite pasar más tiempo a alta intensidad que el entrenamiento continuo.

q: What is circuit training?
o: A series of exercises done one after another with little rest
e: Circuit training: several stations performed in sequence with short rests, often combining strength and cardio.
s: El entrenamiento en circuito: varias estaciones realizadas en secuencia con descansos cortos, a menudo combinando fuerza y cardio.

q: What is a superset?
o: Two exercises performed back to back without rest, often for opposing muscle groups
e: A superset combines two exercises without rest in between, often agonist and antagonist (e.g. biceps curl + triceps extension).
s: Una superserie combina dos ejercicios sin descanso entre ellos, a menudo agonista y antagonista (p. ej., curl de bíceps + extensión de tríceps).

q: What is the main purpose of a warm-up?
o: To burn as many calories as possible
To tire the muscles before training
To prepare body and mind for exercise and reduce injury risk
e: A warm-up raises body and muscle temperature and heart rate, improves mobility and coordination, and prepares mentally.
s: El calentamiento eleva la temperatura corporal y muscular y la frecuencia cardíaca, mejora la movilidad y la coordinación y prepara mentalmente.

q: How long should a general warm-up typically last?
e: A typical warm-up lasts about 5–15 minutes, longer in cold conditions or before intense efforts.
s: Un calentamiento típico dura unos 5–15 minutos, más en condiciones frías o antes de esfuerzos intensos.

q: Which type of stretching is best suited to a warm-up?
e: Dynamic stretching (controlled movements through the range) prepares muscles without the temporary drop in strength that long static holds can cause.
s: El estiramiento dinámico (movimientos controlados en todo el rango) prepara los músculos sin la pérdida temporal de fuerza que pueden provocar los estiramientos estáticos largos.

q: What is the purpose of a cool-down?
o: To gradually bring heart rate and breathing back to rest
e: A cool-down gradually lowers heart rate and breathing and helps avoid blood pooling and dizziness after intense exercise.
s: La vuelta a la calma reduce poco a poco la frecuencia cardíaca y la respiración y ayuda a evitar la acumulación de sangre y los mareos tras un ejercicio intenso.

q: What does PNF stretching stand for?
e: PNF = Proprioceptive Neuromuscular Facilitation: contract-relax techniques to increase range of motion.
s: PNF = Facilitación Neuromuscular Propioceptiva: técnicas de contracción-relajación para aumentar la amplitud de movimiento.

q: How long is a static stretch typically held to improve flexibility?
e: Hold static stretches about 15–30 seconds (up to 60 for older adults), to mild tension, never pain.
s: Mantén los estiramientos estáticos unos 15–30 segundos (hasta 60 en personas mayores), hasta una tensión leve, nunca dolor.

q: What is the recommended minimum amount of moderate-intensity physical activity for adults per week (WHO)?
e: WHO: at least 150–300 minutes of moderate (or 75–150 min vigorous) activity per week, plus muscle-strengthening activities on 2 or more days.
s: OMS: al menos 150–300 minutos de actividad moderada (o 75–150 min vigorosa) por semana, más ejercicios de fortalecimiento muscular 2 o más días.

q: How often per week does the WHO recommend muscle-strengthening activities for adults?
e: Adults should do muscle-strengthening activities involving all major muscle groups on 2 or more days a week.
s: Los adultos deben realizar actividades de fortalecimiento de todos los grupos musculares principales 2 o más días a la semana.

q: In a training programme, in which order should exercises usually be performed?
o: Small muscle groups first, then large
Large, multi-joint exercises first, then small, single-joint exercises
e: Do complex multi-joint exercises (squat, deadlift) while fresh, then smaller isolation exercises.
s: Haz los ejercicios complejos multiarticulares (sentadilla, peso muerto) cuando estás fresco y después los ejercicios de aislamiento más pequeños.

q: Which is an example of a compound (multi-joint) exercise?
e: A squat involves hip, knee and ankle. A biceps curl, leg extension and calf raise involve one joint each.
s: La sentadilla implica cadera, rodilla y tobillo. El curl de bíceps, la extensión de pierna y la elevación de talones implican una sola articulación cada uno.

q: What is the minimum recovery time usually advised before training the same muscle group heavily again?
e: After an intensive session a muscle group generally needs about 48 hours (48–72) to recover.
s: Tras una sesión intensa, un grupo muscular necesita en general unas 48 horas (48–72) para recuperarse.

q: What does 'tempo 3-1-1' in strength training typically mean?
o: 3 seconds eccentric, 1 second pause, 1 second concentric
e: Tempo notation describes the seconds per phase, usually starting with the eccentric (lowering) phase.
s: La notación de tempo describe los segundos por fase, normalmente empezando por la fase excéntrica (bajada).

q: Which heart rate zone (as % of HRmax) is generally considered moderate intensity aerobic training?
e: Moderate intensity is roughly 64–76% of HRmax (ACSM). Vigorous is about 77–95%.
s: La intensidad moderada es aproximadamente el 64–76% de la FCmáx (ACSM). La vigorosa es aproximadamente el 77–95%.

q: Which training method is best for improving aerobic endurance in a beginner?
e: Beginners build aerobic endurance safely with continuous moderate-intensity training (e.g. brisk walking, cycling, easy jogging).
s: Los principiantes desarrollan la resistencia aeróbica con seguridad mediante entrenamiento continuo de intensidad moderada (p. ej., caminar rápido, bici, trote suave).

q: What is plyometric training?
o: Explosive jumping/throwing using the stretch-shortening cycle
e: Plyometrics use a rapid eccentric then concentric action (stretch-shortening cycle) to develop power, e.g. box jumps.
s: La pliometría usa una acción excéntrica rápida seguida de una concéntrica (ciclo de estiramiento-acortamiento) para desarrollar potencia, p. ej., saltos al cajón.

q: A client wants to lose fat. Which advice is most evidence-based?
o: Create an energy deficit with a combination of nutrition, cardio and strength training
Sweat as much as possible in a sauna suit
Only do abdominal exercises to burn belly fat
Only train in the fat-burning zone
e: Fat loss requires an energy deficit. Spot reduction does not work. Strength training helps preserve muscle mass during the deficit.
s: La pérdida de grasa requiere un déficit energético. La reducción localizada no funciona. El entrenamiento de fuerza ayuda a conservar la masa muscular durante el déficit.

q: Which statement about training older adults is correct?
o: They do not adapt to training anymore
Strength and balance training help prevent falls and preserve muscle mass
Strength training is dangerous for them
e: Older adults still adapt. Strength and balance training reduce fall risk and counter sarcopenia (age-related muscle loss).
s: Las personas mayores siguen adaptándose. El entrenamiento de fuerza y equilibrio reduce el riesgo de caídas y combate la sarcopenia (pérdida muscular por la edad).

q: What is sarcopenia?
o: Age-related loss of muscle mass and strength
e: Sarcopenia is the age-related loss of muscle mass and strength. Loss of bone density is osteoporosis.
s: La sarcopenia es la pérdida de masa y fuerza muscular asociada a la edad. La pérdida de densidad ósea es la osteoporosis.

q: What is the 'Valsalva manoeuvre'?
o: Holding your breath and pressing against a closed airway, which raises blood pressure
e: Breath-holding while straining strongly raises blood pressure. Clients with high blood pressure or heart problems should avoid it: breathe out during the effort.
s: Contener la respiración mientras se hace fuerza eleva mucho la presión arterial. Los clientes con hipertensión o problemas cardíacos deben evitarlo: espirar durante el esfuerzo.

q: When should a client exhale during a strength exercise?
o: Only at the end of the set
e: Exhale during the effort (e.g. pushing the bar up), inhale during the lowering phase.
s: Espira durante el esfuerzo (p. ej., al empujar la barra hacia arriba) e inspira durante la fase de bajada.

q: Which substance provides the most energy per gram?
e: Fat ≈ 9 kcal/g, alcohol ≈ 7 kcal/g, carbohydrate (incl. sugar) and protein ≈ 4 kcal/g.
s: Grasa ≈ 9 kcal/g, alcohol ≈ 7 kcal/g, carbohidratos (incl. azúcar) y proteína ≈ 4 kcal/g.

q: What are proteins important for?
o: For building and maintaining the skeleton
For the maintenance of muscles, tendons and ligaments
e: Proteins are the building material of the body: they build and repair muscles, tendons, ligaments, enzymes and hormones. Energy supply is mainly the job of carbohydrates and fats.
s: Las proteínas son el material de construcción del cuerpo: forman y reparan músculos, tendones, ligamentos, enzimas y hormonas. El aporte de energía es sobre todo función de los carbohidratos y las grasas.

q: What can happen to an athlete if he loses 3% of his body fluids during a sports performance due to perspiration?
e: From about 2% fluid loss, performance (endurance and strength) measurably drops. Loss of consciousness and serious heat problems occur with much larger losses.
s: A partir de una pérdida de líquido de aproximadamente el 2%, el rendimiento (resistencia y fuerza) baja de forma medible. La pérdida de consciencia y los problemas graves por calor ocurren con pérdidas mucho mayores.

q: How many kcal does 1 gram of carbohydrate provide?
e: Carbohydrate 4 kcal/g, protein 4 kcal/g, alcohol 7 kcal/g, fat 9 kcal/g.
s: Carbohidrato 4 kcal/g, proteína 4 kcal/g, alcohol 7 kcal/g, grasa 9 kcal/g.

q: How many kcal does 1 gram of protein provide?
e: Protein provides about 4 kcal per gram, the same as carbohydrate.
s: La proteína aporta unas 4 kcal por gramo, igual que los carbohidratos.

q: How many kcal does 1 gram of alcohol provide?
e: Alcohol provides about 7 kcal per gram but no useful nutrients ('empty calories').
s: El alcohol aporta unas 7 kcal por gramo pero ningún nutriente útil ('calorías vacías').

q: Which three nutrients are the macronutrients that provide energy?
e: The energy-providing macronutrients are carbohydrates, fats and proteins. Vitamins and minerals are micronutrients and provide no energy.
s: Los macronutrientes que aportan energía son los carbohidratos, las grasas y las proteínas. Las vitaminas y los minerales son micronutrientes y no aportan energía.

q: Which nutrient is the body's preferred fuel during high-intensity exercise?
e: At high intensity carbohydrates (glycogen, glucose) are the main fuel because they can be broken down quickly, also anaerobically.
s: A alta intensidad los carbohidratos (glucógeno, glucosa) son el combustible principal porque se descomponen rápido, incluso de forma anaeróbica.

q: What is the recommended daily protein intake for a sedentary healthy adult?
o: About 0.8 g per kg body weight
e: The general recommendation is about 0.8 g/kg/day. Strength athletes often benefit from about 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day.
s: La recomendación general es de unos 0,8 g/kg/día. Los deportistas de fuerza suelen beneficiarse de unos 1,6–2,2 g/kg/día.

q: What protein intake is commonly advised for strength athletes who want to build muscle?
e: Research (e.g. ISSN position stand) supports about 1.4–2.0 g/kg/day, with benefit plateauing around 1.6–2.2 g/kg.
s: La investigación (p. ej., la posición de la ISSN) respalda unos 1,4–2,0 g/kg/día, y el beneficio se estabiliza alrededor de 1,6–2,2 g/kg.

q: What are amino acids?
e: Proteins are chains of amino acids. Essential amino acids must come from food because the body cannot make them.
s: Las proteínas son cadenas de aminoácidos. Los aminoácidos esenciales deben venir de los alimentos porque el cuerpo no puede fabricarlos.

q: How many essential amino acids are there?
e: There are 20 amino acids in protein; 9 are essential (must come from the diet).
s: Hay 20 aminoácidos en las proteínas; 9 son esenciales (deben venir de la dieta).

q: Which fats are considered the healthiest?
e: Unsaturated fats (olive oil, nuts, oily fish) support heart health. Trans fats are the most harmful; saturated fats should be limited.
s: Las grasas insaturadas (aceite de oliva, frutos secos, pescado azul) favorecen la salud cardiovascular. Las grasas trans son las más perjudiciales; las saturadas deben limitarse.

q: Omega-3 fatty acids are found mainly in...
o: Oily fish such as salmon and mackerel
e: Oily fish, walnuts and flaxseed are rich in omega-3, a polyunsaturated fat.
s: El pescado azul, las nueces y la linaza son ricos en omega-3, una grasa poliinsaturada.

q: Which vitamins are fat-soluble?
e: Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat-soluble and can be stored in the body. B vitamins and vitamin C are water-soluble.
s: Las vitaminas A, D, E y K son liposolubles y se pueden almacenar en el cuerpo. Las vitaminas B y la vitamina C son hidrosolubles.

q: Which mineral is most important for strong bones?
e: Calcium (together with vitamin D for absorption) is essential for bone strength.
s: El calcio (junto con la vitamina D para su absorción) es esencial para la fortaleza de los huesos.

q: Which mineral is needed for oxygen transport in the blood?
e: Iron is part of haemoglobin, which carries oxygen. Iron deficiency causes fatigue and lower endurance.
s: El hierro forma parte de la hemoglobina, que transporta el oxígeno. La falta de hierro causa cansancio y menor resistencia.

q: Which vitamin is made in the skin under the influence of sunlight?
e: Vitamin D is produced in the skin under UV light and helps absorb calcium.
s: La vitamina D se produce en la piel con la luz UV y ayuda a absorber el calcio.

q: What is the main function of dietary fibre?
o: Supporting digestion and bowel function and giving a feeling of fullness
e: Fibre supports bowel function, feeds gut bacteria, slows sugar uptake and helps you feel full. Adults are advised about 30–40 g per day.
s: La fibra favorece el tránsito intestinal, alimenta la flora, ralentiza la absorción de azúcar y aumenta la saciedad. Se recomiendan unos 30–40 g al día para adultos.

q: What does BMR (basal metabolic rate) mean?
o: The energy the body needs at complete rest for basic functions
The maximum energy you can burn
e: BMR is the energy needed at complete rest to keep basic functions going (breathing, circulation, temperature). It is the largest part of daily energy use.
s: El metabolismo basal es la energía necesaria en reposo total para mantener las funciones básicas (respiración, circulación, temperatura). Es la mayor parte del gasto diario.

q: A client wants to lose weight. What is the basic principle?
o: Energy intake lower than energy expenditure
Energy intake higher than energy expenditure
Energy intake equal to energy expenditure
e: Weight loss requires a negative energy balance: you take in less energy than you use.
s: Perder peso requiere un balance energético negativo: ingerir menos energía de la que se gasta.

q: How many kcal is roughly equal to 1 kg of body fat?
e: 1 kg of body fat stores about 7,000–7,700 kcal. (1 lb ≈ 3,500 kcal, a common trap.)
s: 1 kg de grasa corporal almacena unas 7.000–7.700 kcal. (1 libra ≈ 3.500 kcal, una trampa habitual.)

q: What does the glycaemic index (GI) indicate?
o: The amount of fat in a food
The protein quality of a food
The number of calories in a food
How quickly a carbohydrate food raises blood sugar
e: High-GI foods (white bread) raise blood sugar quickly; low-GI foods (lentils, oats) raise it slowly.
s: Los alimentos de IG alto (pan blanco) elevan el azúcar en sangre rápidamente; los de IG bajo (lentejas, avena) lo elevan lentamente.

q: How much water should an average adult drink per day (approximately)?
e: Guidelines (e.g. Voedingscentrum) advise about 1.5–2 litres of fluid per day, more with exercise and heat.
s: Las guías (p. ej., Voedingscentrum) aconsejan unos 1,5–2 litros de líquido al día, más con ejercicio y calor.

q: What is a good way for a client to check hydration?
o: Amount of sweat on the shirt
Colour of the urine (pale yellow is good)
e: Pale, straw-coloured urine indicates good hydration; dark urine suggests dehydration.
s: Una orina de color amarillo pálido indica buena hidratación; una orina oscura sugiere deshidratación.

q: What is the main cause of muscle cramps in endurance sports, according to the traditional explanation taught in many courses?
o: Fluid and electrolyte loss (and muscle fatigue)
e: Cramps are linked to muscle fatigue and to fluid/electrolyte loss through sweat. Current research points mostly to neuromuscular fatigue.
s: Los calambres se relacionan con la fatiga muscular y con la pérdida de líquidos/electrolitos por el sudor. La investigación actual apunta sobre todo a la fatiga neuromuscular.

q: Which electrolyte is lost most through sweat?
e: Sweat contains mostly sodium (salt), plus smaller amounts of potassium.
s: El sudor contiene sobre todo sodio (sal), además de cantidades menores de potasio.

q: What is a good recovery meal after strength training?
o: A combination of protein and carbohydrates
e: Protein (about 20–40 g) supports muscle repair, carbohydrates refill glycogen.
s: La proteína (unos 20–40 g) favorece la reparación muscular y los carbohidratos reponen el glucógeno.

q: Which statement about carbohydrates is correct?
o: They are only found in sugar
They are stored as glycogen in liver and muscles in limited amounts
They are stored without limit in the body
e: Glycogen stores are limited (roughly 400–500 g in total), which is why long efforts need carbohydrate intake.
s: Las reservas de glucógeno son limitadas (unos 400–500 g en total), por eso los esfuerzos largos requieren ingerir carbohidratos.

q: What is the 'Schijf van Vijf' / healthy plate model mainly used for?
o: Giving guidance on a varied and healthy diet
e: The Dutch 'Schijf van Vijf' (Wheel of Five) from the Voedingscentrum shows which food groups to eat for a healthy, varied diet.
s: La 'Schijf van Vijf' (Rueda de Cinco) del Voedingscentrum neerlandés muestra qué grupos de alimentos comer para una dieta sana y variada.

q: What is the main function of carbohydrates?
e: Carbohydrates are mainly an energy source, especially for the brain and for intense exercise.
s: Los carbohidratos son principalmente una fuente de energía, sobre todo para el cerebro y el ejercicio intenso.

q: Which is a complete protein source (contains all essential amino acids)?
e: Animal proteins (eggs, meat, fish, dairy) and soy contain all essential amino acids. Plant sources can be combined to cover them.
s: Las proteínas animales (huevos, carne, pescado, lácteos) y la soja contienen todos los aminoácidos esenciales. Las fuentes vegetales pueden combinarse para cubrirlos.

q: A supplement that has good scientific evidence for improving short, high-intensity performance is...
e: Creatine monohydrate is one of the best-researched supplements: it increases creatine phosphate stores and improves repeated high-intensity efforts.
s: La creatina monohidrato es uno de los suplementos más estudiados: aumenta las reservas de fosfocreatina y mejora los esfuerzos repetidos de alta intensidad.

q: Which nutrient has the largest effect on satiety (feeling full) per kcal?
e: Protein is the most satiating macronutrient and also costs more energy to digest (thermic effect).
s: La proteína es el macronutriente más saciante y además requiere más energía para digerirse (efecto térmico).

q: What does the 'C' of the ICE rule mean?
e: ICE = Ice (cooling), Compression, Elevation. Compression limits swelling after an acute injury such as a sprained ankle.
s: ICE = Ice (hielo/enfriar), Compression (compresión), Elevation (elevación). La compresión limita la hinchazón tras una lesión aguda como un esguince de tobillo.

flag: Answer not confirmed by the portal. Check this one in your course book.
q: While running on the treadmill, a person's ankle breaks. He can no longer stand on it. How long do you have to cool?
e: Following the ICE rule, cool the injured area for about 20 minutes (with a cloth between ice and skin) and call professional help for a suspected fracture. Do not move the ankle.
s: Siguiendo la regla ICE, enfría la zona lesionada unos 20 minutos (con un paño entre el hielo y la piel) y pide ayuda profesional ante una posible fractura. No muevas el tobillo.

q: What does the 'E' of the ICE rule stand for?
e: Elevation: raise the injured limb above heart level to reduce swelling.
s: Elevation (elevación): eleva el miembro lesionado por encima del nivel del corazón para reducir la hinchazón.

q: Why should you never put ice directly on the skin?
e: Direct contact can freeze the skin. Always use a cloth or towel between ice and skin.
s: El contacto directo puede congelar la piel. Usa siempre un paño o toalla entre el hielo y la piel.

q: What is the difference between a sprain and a strain?
o: A strain is always more serious
A sprain is a muscle injury; a strain is a bone injury
A sprain is a ligament injury; a strain is a muscle or tendon injury
e: Sprain = ligament (e.g. ankle sprain). Strain = muscle or tendon (e.g. pulled hamstring). Tip: strain has a 't' for tendon.
s: Esguince (sprain) = ligamento (p. ej., esguince de tobillo). Distensión (strain) = músculo o tendón (p. ej., rotura de isquiotibial). Truco: strain tiene una 't' de tendon.

q: An inflammation of a tendon is called...
e: Tendinitis/tendinopathy is irritation of a tendon, usually due to overload. Bursitis is inflammation of a bursa.
s: La tendinitis/tendinopatía es la irritación de un tendón, normalmente por sobrecarga. La bursitis es la inflamación de una bolsa sinovial.

q: What is the first thing you do when someone collapses in the gym and does not respond?
o: Wait to see if they wake up
Check for danger, then check responsiveness and breathing, and call for help (112)
e: Make sure the area is safe, check responsiveness and breathing, call 112 (or have someone call) and get the AED if they are not breathing normally.
s: Asegúrate de que la zona es segura, comprueba si responde y respira, llama al 112 (o pide que alguien llame) y trae el DEA si no respira con normalidad.

q: What is the emergency number in the Netherlands and most of Europe?
e: 112 is the European emergency number.
s: El 112 es el número de emergencias europeo.

q: What does AED stand for?
e: AED = Automated External Defibrillator. It analyses heart rhythm and gives a shock if needed.
s: DEA = Desfibrilador Externo Automático. Analiza el ritmo cardíaco y da una descarga si es necesario.

q: What is the ratio of chest compressions to rescue breaths in adult CPR?
e: Adult CPR: 30 chest compressions followed by 2 rescue breaths, at 100–120 compressions per minute.
s: RCP en adultos: 30 compresiones torácicas seguidas de 2 insuflaciones, a 100–120 compresiones por minuto.

q: A diabetic client feels shaky, sweaty and confused during training. What is most likely happening?
e: These are signs of hypoglycaemia. Stop the exercise and give fast-acting sugar (e.g. glucose tablets, lemonade).
s: Son signos de hipoglucemia. Detén el ejercicio y da azúcar de acción rápida (p. ej., tabletas de glucosa, refresco azucarado).

q: Which symptom during exercise is a reason to stop immediately?
o: Muscle fatigue at the end of a set
e: Chest pain, severe breathlessness, dizziness, fainting or irregular heartbeat are warning signs: stop and seek medical help.
s: El dolor u opresión en el pecho, la falta de aire intensa, los mareos, el desmayo o el latido irregular son señales de alarma: detén el ejercicio y busca ayuda médica.

q: A client faints in the gym but is breathing normally. What position do you put them in?
e: An unresponsive person who is breathing normally goes in the recovery position to keep the airway open. Call 112 and keep checking breathing.
s: Una persona inconsciente que respira con normalidad se coloca en posición lateral de seguridad para mantener la vía aérea abierta. Llama al 112 y sigue comprobando la respiración.

q: What is the main purpose of the ICE rule after an acute injury?
e: Cooling, compression and elevation limit swelling, internal bleeding and pain in the first phase after an acute injury.
s: Enfriar, comprimir y elevar limitan la hinchazón, la hemorragia interna y el dolor en la primera fase tras una lesión aguda.

q: What is an acute injury?
o: An injury of the skin only
An injury that develops slowly through repeated overload
An injury that happens suddenly due to a single event
e: Acute injury: sudden, clear moment (sprain, fracture). Overuse injury: gradual, from repeated overload (tendinopathy, shin splints).
s: Lesión aguda: repentina, con un momento claro (esguince, fractura). Lesión por sobrecarga: gradual, por sobrecarga repetida (tendinopatía, periostitis tibial).

q: Which is an example of an overuse injury?
e: Shin splints (medial tibial stress syndrome) develop gradually through repeated overload, typically in runners.
s: La periostitis tibial (síndrome de estrés tibial medial) se desarrolla gradualmente por sobrecarga repetida, típicamente en corredores.

q: How can a fitness trainer best prevent overuse injuries in clients?
o: Train the same exercise every day
Build up load gradually and plan enough recovery
e: Gradual progression with adequate recovery keeps load within load capacity, which prevents overload.
s: Una progresión gradual con recuperación suficiente mantiene la carga dentro de la capacidad de carga, lo que previene la sobrecarga.

q: What is the safest action when you notice a broken or faulty machine in the gym?
o: Put it out of use (mark it) and report it immediately
Tell clients to avoid it only if they ask
Fix it yourself during a session
e: Mark the equipment as out of order, prevent use and report it so it can be repaired. This is part of your duty of care.
s: Marca el equipo como fuera de servicio, impide su uso e infórmalo para que se repare. Forma parte de tu deber de cuidado.

q: What is the best way to prevent clients from being injured by free weights lying on the floor?
o: Leave them; clients will see them
Keep the training area tidy and put weights back in the rack
e: A tidy training floor prevents tripping and falling. Encourage clients to rack weights after use.
s: Una zona de entrenamiento ordenada evita tropiezos y caídas. Anima a los clientes a devolver los pesos a su sitio.

q: A client has high blood pressure (hypertension). What should you avoid?
o: Holding the breath and very heavy isometric efforts (Valsalva)
e: Breath-holding and very heavy straining raise blood pressure sharply. Moderate aerobic and dynamic strength training with proper breathing are recommended.
s: Contener la respiración y los esfuerzos muy pesados elevan bruscamente la presión arterial. Se recomienda entrenamiento aeróbico moderado y de fuerza dinámica con buena respiración.

q: What is a contra-indication?
o: A reason why a certain exercise or training should not be done
e: A contra-indication is a condition or factor that makes a treatment or exercise inadvisable (e.g. exercise with a fever).
s: Una contraindicación es una condición o factor que hace desaconsejable un tratamiento o ejercicio (p. ej., hacer ejercicio con fiebre).

q: A client has a fever. What do you advise?
o: Train hard to sweat it out
Do not train until the fever has gone
e: Exercising with a fever is a contra-indication: it increases the risk of heart muscle inflammation (myocarditis). Rest until recovered.
s: Hacer ejercicio con fiebre está contraindicado: aumenta el riesgo de inflamación del músculo cardíaco (miocarditis). Descansar hasta recuperarse.

q: What are the classic signs of inflammation?
o: Redness, heat, swelling, pain and loss of function
e: The five classic signs: rubor (redness), calor (heat), tumor (swelling), dolor (pain) and functio laesa (loss of function).
s: Los cinco signos clásicos: rubor (enrojecimiento), calor, tumor (hinchazón), dolor y functio laesa (pérdida de función).

q: What is heat stroke?
o: A muscle cramp due to heat
A life-threatening rise in body temperature where the body can no longer cool itself
e: Heat stroke: core temperature above about 40 °C with confusion. Call 112 and cool the person down immediately.
s: Golpe de calor: temperatura central por encima de unos 40 °C con confusión. Llama al 112 y enfría a la persona inmediatamente.

q: Who is responsible for creating a safe training environment during a personal training session?
e: The trainer has a duty of care: check equipment, space, technique and the client's health status.
s: El entrenador tiene un deber de cuidado: revisar el equipo, el espacio, la técnica y el estado de salud del cliente.

q: A client with lower back pain asks for advice. What is the right action for a fitness trainer?
o: Diagnose the cause and treat it
Refer to a (sports) physiotherapist or doctor if pain is unexplained, severe or persistent
Tell them to rest for 6 weeks
e: A fitness trainer does not diagnose. Refer to a medical professional when needed and stay within your scope of practice.
s: Un entrenador de fitness no diagnostica. Deriva a un profesional sanitario cuando sea necesario y mantente dentro de tus competencias.

q: What is a common sign of dehydration?
o: Dark urine, thirst, headache and fatigue
e: Dark urine, thirst, headache, dizziness and fatigue indicate dehydration.
s: La orina oscura, la sed, el dolor de cabeza, los mareos y la fatiga indican deshidratación.

q: What is the main risk of a cool-down that is skipped after very intensive exercise?
o: Blood pooling in the legs, which can cause dizziness or fainting
e: Stopping suddenly removes the muscle pump; blood can pool in the legs and blood pressure drops, causing dizziness.
s: Parar de golpe elimina la bomba muscular; la sangre puede acumularse en las piernas y la presión arterial cae, lo que provoca mareos.

q: A client who is pregnant wants to continue training. Which advice is correct?
o: Train only lying on the stomach
With medical approval, moderate exercise is generally recommended; avoid lying flat on the back for long periods later in pregnancy and avoid contact/fall risks
e: Guidelines (ACOG, WHO) recommend moderate activity during an uncomplicated pregnancy, avoiding fall/contact risk and prolonged supine positions after the first trimester.
s: Las guías (ACOG, OMS) recomiendan actividad moderada en un embarazo sin complicaciones, evitando el riesgo de caídas/contacto y la posición boca arriba prolongada después del primer trimestre.

q: What does 'scope of practice' mean for a fitness trainer?
o: The tasks a trainer is qualified and allowed to do
e: A fitness trainer advises on exercise and general healthy lifestyle; diagnosing injuries, prescribing diets for medical conditions or treating are outside the scope.
s: Un entrenador de fitness asesora sobre ejercicio y estilo de vida saludable en general; diagnosticar lesiones, prescribir dietas para enfermedades o tratar quedan fuera de sus competencias.

q: Which client should you refer to a doctor before starting a training programme?
o: A client who already runs twice a week
A client who wants to lose 2 kg
A client who answers 'yes' to one or more PAR-Q questions
e: A 'yes' on the PAR-Q indicates a possible health risk; ask for medical clearance first.
s: Un 'sí' en el PAR-Q indica un posible riesgo para la salud; pide primero autorización médica.

q: Which factor increases the risk of cardiovascular disease?
e: Risk factors include smoking, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, diabetes, obesity, inactivity and family history.
s: Los factores de riesgo incluyen fumar, hipertensión, colesterol alto, diabetes, obesidad, inactividad y antecedentes familiares.

q: PAR-Q stands for?
e: PAR-Q = Physical Activity Readiness Questionnaire: a short health screening to see if someone can safely start exercising or needs medical clearance first.
s: PAR-Q = Cuestionario de Aptitud para la Actividad Física: un breve cribado de salud para ver si alguien puede empezar a hacer ejercicio con seguridad o necesita antes autorización médica.

q: The Cooper test measures the distance that can be covered in how many minutes?
e: The Cooper test is a 12-minute run for maximum distance, used to estimate VO2max (aerobic fitness).
s: El test de Cooper es una carrera de 12 minutos para recorrer la máxima distancia; se usa para estimar el VO2max (capacidad aeróbica).

q: How is BMI calculated?
e: BMI = body weight in kg divided by height in metres squared.
s: IMC = peso corporal en kg dividido por la altura en metros al cuadrado.

q: A client weighs 80 kg and is 2.00 m tall. What is the BMI?
A BMI between 25 and 30 is classified as...
e: WHO: below 18.5 underweight; 18.5–24.9 healthy; 25–29.9 overweight; 30 or more obese.
s: OMS: menos de 18,5 bajo peso; 18,5–24,9 peso saludable; 25–29,9 sobrepeso; 30 o más obesidad.

q: From what BMI is someone classified as obese?
e: A BMI of 30 or higher is classified as obesity.
s: Un IMC de 30 o más se clasifica como obesidad.

q: What is an important limitation of BMI?
o: It does not distinguish between muscle mass and fat mass
e: A muscular athlete can have a high BMI without excess fat. BMI says nothing about body composition or fat distribution.
s: Un deportista musculoso puede tener un IMC alto sin exceso de grasa. El IMC no dice nada de la composición corporal ni de la distribución de la grasa.

q: Which waist circumference indicates an increased health risk for a man (European guideline)?
e: Men: increased risk above 94 cm, substantially increased above 102 cm. Women: above 80 cm and 88 cm.
s: Hombres: riesgo aumentado por encima de 94 cm, muy aumentado por encima de 102 cm. Mujeres: por encima de 80 cm y 88 cm.

q: Which waist circumference indicates an increased health risk for a woman?
e: Women: increased risk above 80 cm, substantially increased above 88 cm.
s: Mujeres: riesgo aumentado por encima de 80 cm, muy aumentado por encima de 88 cm.

q: Why is waist circumference a useful measurement?
o: It indicates abdominal (visceral) fat, which is linked to health risks
e: Abdominal fat around the organs is strongly linked to cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes.
s: La grasa abdominal alrededor de los órganos está fuertemente relacionada con las enfermedades cardiovasculares y la diabetes tipo 2.

q: Which method measures body fat percentage using skinfold thickness?
e: A skinfold calliper measures subcutaneous fat at fixed sites; formulas then estimate body fat percentage.
s: Un plicómetro mide la grasa subcutánea en puntos fijos; después se estima el porcentaje de grasa con fórmulas.

q: What does bio-electrical impedance analysis (BIA) measure?
o: Body composition (estimate of fat %) via a small electrical current
e: BIA sends a weak current through the body; fat conducts less than muscle/water. Results depend strongly on hydration.
s: La BIA envía una corriente débil por el cuerpo; la grasa conduce peor que el músculo/agua. Los resultados dependen mucho de la hidratación.

q: What is the purpose of an intake (anamnesis) with a new client?
o: To gather information about health, history, goals and wishes to make a safe, personal programme
e: The intake collects health status, injuries, medication, lifestyle, experience and goals as the basis for a safe and personal plan.
s: La entrevista inicial recoge estado de salud, lesiones, medicación, estilo de vida, experiencia y objetivos como base de un plan seguro y personalizado.

q: Where is the best place to measure the heart rate manually?
o: At the wrist (radial artery) or neck (carotid artery)
e: The radial pulse (wrist, thumb side) or carotid pulse (neck) are used. Use fingers, not your thumb, and press lightly on the carotid.
s: Se usa el pulso radial (muñeca, lado del pulgar) o el carotídeo (cuello). Usa los dedos, no el pulgar, y presiona suavemente la carótida.

q: When is the best moment to measure resting heart rate?
o: In the morning after waking, before getting up
e: True resting heart rate is measured in the morning, lying down, just after waking.
s: La frecuencia cardíaca en reposo real se mide por la mañana, tumbado, justo al despertar.

q: What does the sit-and-reach test measure?
o: Flexibility of the hamstrings and lower back
e: The sit-and-reach test measures flexibility of the hamstrings and lower back.
s: El test de sit-and-reach mide la flexibilidad de los isquiotibiales y la zona lumbar.

q: What does a push-up test mainly measure?
o: Muscular endurance of the upper body
e: Push-ups to fatigue measure muscular endurance of the chest, shoulders and triceps.
s: Las flexiones hasta el fallo miden la resistencia muscular del pecho, hombros y tríceps.

q: Which test is used to estimate aerobic capacity on a bicycle ergometer?
e: The Astrand(-Ryhming) test uses a submaximal cycling workload and the heart rate to estimate VO2max.
s: El test de Astrand(-Ryhming) usa una carga submáxima en bicicleta y la frecuencia cardíaca para estimar el VO2max.

q: What is a submaximal test?
o: A test where the client works below maximal effort and the maximum is estimated
A test where the client works to complete exhaustion
e: Submaximal tests are safer for untrained clients: the maximum (e.g. VO2max or 1RM) is estimated from a lower effort.
s: Los tests submáximos son más seguros para clientes no entrenados: el máximo (p. ej., VO2max o 1RM) se estima a partir de un esfuerzo menor.

q: Why should you retest a client after some weeks?
o: Because the first test is always wrong
To evaluate progress and adjust the programme
