e: Retesting (same conditions, same protocol) shows progress, motivates the client and guides programme changes.
s: Repetir el test (mismas condiciones, mismo protocolo) muestra el progreso, motiva al cliente y orienta los cambios del programa.

q: What makes a test 'reliable'?
o: It gives the same result when repeated under the same conditions
It measures what it is supposed to measure
e: Reliability = reproducibility (same result on repetition). Validity = it measures what it claims to measure.
s: Fiabilidad = reproducibilidad (mismo resultado al repetir). Validez = mide lo que dice medir.

q: What makes a test 'valid'?
o: It measures what it is intended to measure
It gives the same result every time
e: Validity: the test measures the quality it intends to measure (e.g. the Cooper test for aerobic endurance).
s: Validez: el test mide la cualidad que pretende medir (p. ej., el test de Cooper para la resistencia aeróbica).

q: During a posture analysis you see an increased hollow in the lower back. This is called...
e: An increased lumbar curve is hyperlordosis, often with an anterior pelvic tilt.
s: Una curva lumbar aumentada es hiperlordosis, a menudo con inclinación pélvica anterior.

q: Hyperlordosis is often associated with...
o: Anterior pelvic tilt with tight hip flexors
e: Tight hip flexors and lower back muscles with weak abdominals and glutes tilt the pelvis forward (lower crossed syndrome).
s: Los flexores de cadera y lumbares acortados con abdominales y glúteos débiles inclinan la pelvis hacia delante (síndrome cruzado inferior).

q: A client has rounded shoulders and a forward head. Which muscles are usually tight?
e: Upper crossed syndrome: tight chest and upper trapezius, weak deep neck flexors, rhomboids and lower trapezius.
s: Síndrome cruzado superior: pectoral y trapecio superior acortados; flexores profundos del cuello, romboides y trapecio inferior débiles.

q: From which views do you carry out a static posture analysis?
o: From the front, side and back
e: A static posture analysis is done from the front (anterior), side (lateral) and back (posterior), often with a plumb line.
s: El análisis postural estático se hace de frente (anterior), de lado (lateral) y de espaldas (posterior), a menudo con una plomada.

q: In a side view of good posture, the plumb line runs through...
o: Ear, shoulder, hip, slightly in front of the knee and in front of the ankle
Nose, navel and between the feet
e: Lateral view: earlobe – shoulder (acromion) – hip (greater trochanter) – just in front of the knee – just in front of the lateral ankle.
s: Vista lateral: lóbulo de la oreja – hombro (acromion) – cadera (trocánter mayor) – justo delante de la rodilla – justo delante del maléolo externo.

q: What is 'informed consent'?
o: The client's permission after being informed about the training, risks and tests
e: Informed consent: the client agrees in writing after being clearly told what the training/tests involve and their possible risks.
s: Consentimiento informado: el cliente acepta por escrito después de ser informado claramente de lo que implican el entrenamiento/los tests y sus posibles riesgos.

q: What does a 1RM test measure?
e: A 1RM test measures maximal dynamic strength. For beginners, estimate 1RM from a submaximal set (e.g. 10RM) instead.
s: Un test de 1RM mide la fuerza máxima dinámica. Para principiantes, estima el 1RM a partir de una serie submáxima (p. ej., 10RM).

q: What does a hand grip dynamometer measure?
e: The hand grip test measures isometric grip strength, a good indicator of overall strength and health in older adults.
s: El test de dinamometría de mano mide la fuerza isométrica de agarre, buen indicador de fuerza general y salud en personas mayores.

q: Which test measures balance?
e: The stork stand test measures static balance: how long a person can stand on one leg.
s: El test de la cigüeña mide el equilibrio estático: cuánto tiempo puede mantenerse una persona sobre una pierna.

q: Before which of these tests is a PAR-Q especially important?
e: Maximal and strenuous tests put high demands on heart and circulation, so health screening beforehand is essential.
s: Los tests máximos y exigentes suponen una gran carga para el corazón y la circulación, por eso es esencial el cribado de salud previo.

q: The transtheoretical model has .. stages?
e: The transtheoretical model (Prochaska & DiClemente) has 5 stages: precontemplation, contemplation, preparation, action and maintenance. Some versions add a 6th (termination) or relapse, but the course answer is 5.
s: El modelo transteórico (Prochaska y DiClemente) tiene 5 etapas: precontemplación, contemplación, preparación, acción y mantenimiento. Algunas versiones añaden una 6ª (finalización) o la recaída, pero la respuesta del curso es 5.

q: Which is the correct order of the stages of change (transtheoretical model)?
e: Precontemplation (not thinking about it) → contemplation (thinking about it) → preparation (planning) → action (doing it < 6 months) → maintenance (> 6 months).
s: Precontemplación (no lo piensa) → contemplación (lo piensa) → preparación (planifica) → acción (lo hace < 6 meses) → mantenimiento (> 6 meses).

q: A client says: 'I know I should exercise more and I'm thinking about starting in the next few months.' Which stage is this?
e: Contemplation: the person is considering change within about 6 months but has not taken steps yet.
s: Contemplación: la persona considera cambiar en unos 6 meses pero aún no ha dado pasos.

q: A client has been training regularly for 8 months. Which stage of change is this?
e: Maintenance = new behaviour kept up for more than 6 months. Action = less than 6 months.
s: Mantenimiento = nuevo comportamiento mantenido más de 6 meses. Acción = menos de 6 meses.

q: A client has just bought sports shoes and signed up for the gym starting next week. Which stage is this?
e: Preparation: the person intends to act soon (within a month) and is taking small steps.
s: Preparación: la persona tiene intención de actuar pronto (en un mes) y está dando pequeños pasos.

q: A person says: 'Exercise isn't for me, I don't see why I would.' Which stage is this?
e: Precontemplation: no intention to change in the foreseeable future, often unaware of or denying the problem.
s: Precontemplación: no hay intención de cambiar en un futuro próximo, a menudo sin ser consciente del problema o negándolo.

q: What does the 'S' in SMART goals stand for?
e: SMART = Specific, Measurable, Acceptable/Achievable, Realistic, Time-bound.
s: SMART = Específico, Medible, Aceptable/Alcanzable, Realista, con plazo (Time-bound).

q: What does the 'T' in SMART stand for?
e: Time-bound: the goal has a clear deadline, e.g. 'within 12 weeks'.
s: Time-bound: el objetivo tiene una fecha límite clara, p. ej., 'en 12 semanas'.

q: Which goal is formulated SMART?
o: I want to look better on the beach
I want to lose weight soon
I want to run 5 km without walking within 10 weeks, training 3 times per week
e: Only this goal is specific, measurable, realistic and has a deadline.
s: Solo este objetivo es específico, medible, realista y tiene una fecha límite.

q: What is intrinsic motivation?
o: Motivation from within, because the activity itself is enjoyable or meaningful
Motivation caused by pressure from others
Motivation from rewards such as money or prizes
e: Intrinsic motivation comes from inside (enjoyment, interest). It predicts long-term exercise adherence better than extrinsic motivation.
s: La motivación intrínseca viene de dentro (disfrute, interés). Predice mejor la adherencia al ejercicio a largo plazo que la motivación extrínseca.

q: Which is an example of extrinsic motivation?
o: Liking the challenge of learning a new skill
Training to win a bet or to please others
e: Extrinsic motivation comes from outside rewards or pressure (money, prizes, approval).
s: La motivación extrínseca viene de recompensas o presiones externas (dinero, premios, aprobación).

q: According to Self-Determination Theory, which three basic needs support motivation?
e: Self-Determination Theory (Deci & Ryan): autonomy (own choice), competence (feeling capable) and relatedness (connection with others).
s: Teoría de la Autodeterminación (Deci y Ryan): autonomía (elección propia), competencia (sentirse capaz) y relación (conexión con otros).

q: How can a trainer support a client's autonomy?
o: Give the client choices and involve them in decisions
e: Offering choices and explaining the 'why' supports autonomy and long-term motivation.
s: Ofrecer opciones y explicar el 'porqué' favorece la autonomía y la motivación a largo plazo.

q: What is an open question?
o: A question with multiple choice answers
A question that can be answered with yes or no
A question that invites the client to explain in their own words
e: Open questions (what, how, which) start a conversation, e.g. 'How did your week of training go?'
s: Las preguntas abiertas (qué, cómo, cuál) inician una conversación, p. ej., '¿Cómo te fue la semana de entrenamiento?'

q: Which is an example of a closed question?
o: How do you feel about your progress?
What makes training difficult for you?
What would you like to achieve?
e: A closed question can be answered with yes/no or a single fact.
s: Una pregunta cerrada se puede responder con sí/no o con un solo dato.

q: What does 'active listening' include?
o: Paying full attention, summarising and asking follow-up questions
e: Active listening: attention (eye contact, nodding), summarising, paraphrasing and asking further (in Dutch: LSD – Luisteren, Samenvatten, Doorvragen).
s: Escucha activa: atención (contacto visual, asentir), resumir, parafrasear y seguir preguntando (en neerlandés: LSD – Luisteren, Samenvatten, Doorvragen).

q: In the Dutch communication technique 'LSD', what does the 'S' stand for?
e: LSD = Luisteren (listen), Samenvatten (summarise), Doorvragen (ask further).
s: LSD = Luisteren (escuchar), Samenvatten (resumir), Doorvragen (seguir preguntando).

q: Which percentage of communication is often said to be non-verbal?
o: The largest part (often quoted as about 70–90%)
e: Courses often quote that most communication is non-verbal (body language, tone). The famous '93%' figure comes from Mehrabian's limited studies on feelings, so treat exact numbers with care.
s: Los cursos suelen afirmar que la mayor parte de la comunicación es no verbal (lenguaje corporal, tono). La famosa cifra del '93%' viene de estudios limitados de Mehrabian sobre sentimientos, así que trata las cifras exactas con cuidado.

q: What is the 'sandwich method' of giving feedback?
o: Positive point – point for improvement – positive point
e: The sandwich method wraps a point for improvement between two positives, so feedback is received well.
s: El método sándwich coloca un punto de mejora entre dos aspectos positivos, para que el feedback se reciba bien.

q: Which feedback is most effective for a client learning a new exercise?
o: 'Good, now push your knees outward a little more.'
e: Effective feedback is specific, positive and gives one clear action point at a time.
s: El feedback eficaz es específico, positivo y da un único punto de acción claro cada vez.

q: What are the three stages of motor learning (Fitts & Posner)?
e: Cognitive (understanding, many errors) → associative (refining) → autonomous (automatic, little conscious attention).
s: Cognitiva (comprensión, muchos errores) → asociativa (perfeccionamiento) → autónoma (automática, poca atención consciente).

q: A client is learning a deadlift for the first time and makes many mistakes. Which learning stage is this?
e: In the cognitive stage the learner is figuring out what to do; give simple instructions and limited, clear feedback.
s: En la etapa cognitiva el aprendiz está entendiendo qué hacer; da instrucciones sencillas y un feedback limitado y claro.

q: What is the most effective way to teach a new exercise to a beginner?
o: Let the client figure it out alone
Explain briefly, demonstrate, let the client perform, then give feedback
Give a long theoretical explanation only
e: Tell – show – do – feedback: short explanation, demonstration, practice and specific feedback.
s: Explicar – mostrar – hacer – feedback: explicación breve, demostración, práctica y feedback específico.

q: What is a 'cue' in fitness instruction?
o: A short, clear instruction or signal that helps the client move correctly
e: Cues are short instructions (verbal, visual or tactile), e.g. 'chest up', 'push the floor away'.
s: Las indicaciones (cues) son instrucciones breves (verbales, visuales o táctiles), p. ej., 'pecho arriba', 'empuja el suelo'.

q: Which is an example of a tactile (kinaesthetic) cue?
o: Lightly touching the client's upper back to show where to engage
Writing the exercise on a card
e: Tactile cues use touch; always ask permission first and explain why.
s: Las indicaciones táctiles usan el contacto; pide siempre permiso primero y explica por qué.

q: What is an external focus cue?
e: External focus points attention to the movement's effect on the environment. Research (Wulf) shows it often improves performance and learning compared with internal (body-focused) cues.
s: El foco externo dirige la atención al efecto del movimiento sobre el entorno. La investigación (Wulf) muestra que suele mejorar el rendimiento y el aprendizaje frente a indicaciones internas (centradas en el cuerpo).

q: Where should a trainer stand while instructing a client on a squat?
o: In a position where the trainer can see the movement well and intervene if needed
Always directly in front, touching the client
e: Choose a position (often at a 45° angle to the side) with a good view of the movement and where you can act safely.
s: Elige una posición (a menudo a 45° de lado) con buena visión del movimiento y desde donde puedas actuar con seguridad.

q: What is the most important factor for client retention in a gym?
o: Personal attention, results and a good relationship with staff
e: Clients stay when they feel seen, supported and see progress. Personal contact strongly predicts retention.
s: Los clientes se quedan cuando se sienten vistos, apoyados y ven progreso. El contacto personal predice fuertemente la retención.

q: A client hasn't come to the gym for three weeks. What is the best action?
o: Do nothing; it is their choice
Contact the client in a friendly way to ask how they are and help them restart
e: Proactive, friendly contact shows care and helps the client back into the routine, which improves retention.
s: Un contacto proactivo y amable muestra interés y ayuda al cliente a retomar la rutina, lo que mejora la retención.

q: What is 'self-efficacy' (Bandura)?
o: Belief in one's own ability to successfully perform a behaviour
e: Self-efficacy is confidence in your ability to succeed. It grows mainly through mastery experiences (small successes).
s: La autoeficacia es la confianza en la propia capacidad para tener éxito. Crece sobre todo con experiencias de logro (pequeños éxitos).

q: What is the strongest way to increase a client's self-efficacy?
o: Letting them experience success with achievable tasks
e: Mastery experiences (achieving realistic steps) are the strongest source of self-efficacy.
s: Las experiencias de logro (alcanzar pasos realistas) son la fuente más fuerte de autoeficacia.

q: What is motivational interviewing?
o: A client-centred conversation style that strengthens the client's own motivation for change
A test of motivation with questionnaires
e: Motivational interviewing uses open questions, affirmations, reflections and summaries (OARS) to draw out the client's own reasons for change.
s: La entrevista motivacional usa preguntas abiertas, afirmaciones, reflejos y resúmenes (OARS) para hacer surgir las razones propias del cliente para cambiar.

q: How should a trainer respond to a client in the precontemplation stage?
o: Provide information and raise awareness without pressure
e: In precontemplation, focus on awareness and information about benefits; pushing an action plan rarely works.
s: En la precontemplación, céntrate en la concienciación y en la información sobre los beneficios; imponer un plan de acción rara vez funciona.

q: Which describes good customer service by a fitness trainer?
o: Greeting clients, being approachable and proactive in offering help
Only helping clients who pay extra
e: Being visible, friendly and proactive on the gym floor is the basis of good service and retention.
s: Ser visible, amable y proactivo en la sala es la base de un buen servicio y de la retención.

q: What is the main purpose of evaluating goals with a client regularly?
o: To make the client feel guilty
To monitor progress, celebrate success and adjust the plan
e: Regular evaluation keeps goals relevant, shows progress (motivation) and allows the programme to be adjusted.
s: La evaluación periódica mantiene los objetivos relevantes, muestra el progreso (motivación) y permite ajustar el programa.

q: Which teaching method splits a complex exercise into smaller parts?
e: The part method teaches components separately (e.g. hip hinge before a full clean), then combines them.
s: El método por partes enseña los componentes por separado (p. ej., la bisagra de cadera antes de una cargada completa) y luego los combina.

q: What does 'empathy' mean in client communication?
o: Agreeing with everything the client says
Understanding and acknowledging the client's feelings and perspective
Telling the client your own problems
e: Empathy means understanding the client's situation and showing it, e.g. 'I can imagine that's frustrating.'
s: La empatía es comprender la situación del cliente y demostrarlo, p. ej., 'Me imagino que eso es frustrante.'

q: What is a relapse in the context of behaviour change?
e: Relapse is a return to old behaviour. It is normal; help the client see it as a learning moment and restart.
s: La recaída es volver al comportamiento anterior. Es normal; ayuda al cliente a verla como un aprendizaje y a volver a empezar.
